items.title: Get It While It's Hot: REIT SHOP-ing Spree Continues As Development Grows More Attractive
items.take: Welltower has about $21B of 2026 investment activity done or under contract and Ventas more than $5.2B, as the REITs say development is becoming attractive again.
items.why: Takeout buyers for stabilized AL/MC are deep, which supports the exit assumption in our capital plans.

items.title: Ventas Ups 2026 Acquisition Total to $5.2B With Potentially More to Buy Ahead
items.take: 37 transactions so far in 2026; the operating portfolio now counts 845 properties at 90.2% average occupancy.
items.why: Another buyer for stabilized product at the end of lease-up.

items.title: Welltower Earnings Boosted by Senior Housing Acquisitions
items.take: Welltower bought 43 senior housing properties for $2.7B in Q3; quarterly revenue rose about 38% from a year earlier.
items.why: The largest healthcare REIT keeps adding operating senior housing, which sets pricing for exits.

items.title: Aging Boomers Fuel $28 Billion Investor Rush Into Senior Housing
items.take: Bloomberg reports a $28 billion wave of investor money into senior housing, driven by boomer demographics and returns that outpace other real estate.
items.why: Institutional capital is looking for exactly the product ATCO would build.

items.title: NIC Tracks 88,283 Planned Senior Housing Units in 2026
items.take: 88,283 units are in planning across 214 markets, but only 16,159 are under construction; primary-market occupancy reached 90.4% in Q3.
items.why: Most of the pipeline is still paper. Sites with approvals in hand, like our entitled pads, are scarce.

items.title: In the Pipeline: Sunrise Plans 50 New Projects Targeting Luxury Senior Living; Distinctive Living Sets Groundbreaking Date in New Jersey
items.take: Sunrise plans more than 50 communities ($7.5B) in high-barrier markets including New York City. Distinctive Living breaks ground on CopperWood, 214 units on the former Pfizer campus in Peapack-Gladstone, NJ.
items.why: Sunrise is the contract vendee at Rye Brook and is expanding in our region; CopperWood is a direct Somerset County comp for adaptive reuse.

items.title: Senior Housing Supply Gap Creates More Than $1 Trillion Investment Need Through 2050
items.take: The 80+ population grows about a third by 2030 and nearly doubles by 2040; starts fell about 67% since 2021.
items.why: The demand curve our need scores rely on, from the industry's reference data source.

items.title: In the Pipeline: Distinctive Living Plans Next Development in New Jersey
items.take: CopperWood (118 IL, 66 AL, 30 MC) closed $84.7M of construction financing with Melillo Equities and PointsFive.
items.why: Shows lenders will fund luxury IL/AL/MC conversions of corporate campuses in northern New Jersey.

items.title: 2026 Senior Housing Development Costs
items.take: Across 36 projects, total development cost averaged $388,830 per unit ($364/SF), with an 8.1% average return on cost.
items.why: Our New York-region costs run higher ($440k+ per unit ex-land on AL/MC pads), which is why the 6.5% floor is the right test here.

items.title: U.S. Senior Housing & Care Investor Survey H1 2026
items.take: Cap rates fell about 20 bps in six months; Class A assisted living in core markets is at 6.5%. 82% of respondents expect 3% to 7% rent growth.
items.why: We moved our exit cap to 6.5% to match CBRE's Class A core AL figure; every site shows 6.25–7.00% sensitivity and a +50 bps downside.

items.title: America Faces A Massive Senior Housing Shortage. Wall Street Sees Opportunity
items.take: Investors put $12.1B into senior housing in Q1 2026 (MSCI), the most in at least 20 years; average rents are up 28% since Q4 2020 (JLL).
items.why: Rent growth since 2020 supports the rates in our model.

items.title: Senior Housing Market Q1 2026: Occupancy Nears 90%, Supply Hits Historic Lows
items.take: 19th straight quarterly occupancy gain; IL inventory grew just 0.4% a year, the lowest since 2006. IL at 91.1%, AL at 87.9%.
items.why: A HUD 232 lender's read of the market, which is relevant to our permanent take-out.

items.title: Senior Housing Occupancy Climbs to 89.5% as Record Demand Meets Record-Low New Supply
items.take: About 16,400 units under construction, 2.3% of inventory and the lowest since 2012; NIC expects occupancy above 90% in 2026.
items.why: Low deliveries through 2028 mean little new competition while our projects lease up.

items.title: Investors Bullish on Housing for Older Adults
items.take: JLL: the 80+ population grows 36.6% over the next decade against 5% for the total population; 86% of investors plan to add exposure.
items.why: Demand is concentrated in the 80+ cohort that AL/MC serves.

items.title: Aging Baby Boomers Revive Senior Housing Sector Ravaged by Covid
items.take: Senior living's rebound helped municipal bond defaults fall to their lowest since at least 2009.
items.why: Tax-exempt bond financing for nonprofit-sponsored campuses (the RiverSpring route) is healthy again.

items.title: Emerging Trends in Real Estate 2026
items.take: ULI and PwC put senior housing with data centers among the top growth sectors; the first boomers turn 80 in 2026.
items.why: The industry's leading outlook names senior housing a priority sector.
